flagged.evidence: The current items list contains 26 entries and omits lem-fork-detection-transports-to-arbitrary-boundary-crosscuts, which the scope's page_order_anchors includes among this page's 27 items. The opened kernel-edge lemma lists that omitted supplier in deps and uses it in [F3] and proof 1.1. The page also places lem-closed-lkb-basis-surfaces-have-the-three-required-topological-types-and-factors before its direct dependency lem-the-fork-noodle-pairing-is-well-defined-and-equivariant.

The page states that the covering homomorphism's 'kernel is the deck group'. The opened def-lawrence-krammer-bigelow-cover instead states Deck(C-tilde/C) ≅ π1(C,c0)/ker Φ ≅ im Φ = Z². The kernel classifies the covering and corresponds to its fundamental group; the deck group is the quotient.

The page says the closed surfaces v_{i,j} 'have triangular unit pairings with the dual classes x_{i,j}'. The opened integral-module theorem, proof 1.1, explicitly says the actual absolute-cycle pairing matrix multiplies each relative row by a nonzero closing factor and that 'These factors are not asserted to be Laurent units'. Already at n=2 the diagonal pairing is a Laurent unit times (1-q)²(1+qt)(1-t), which is not a unit: its augmentation q=t=1 is zero. Unit diagonal pairings belong to the relative classes v'_{i,j}.

[F1] places the square and triangle classes in H2(C-tilde,nu-tilde) and then says 'the endpoints may lie in P or on ∂D'. Boundary endpoints require a boundary-relative group. Two disjoint boundary-to-boundary chords, as used in this item's [F2], give a square whose outer boundary lies in ∂C-tilde and need not lie in nu-tilde; it therefore is not the asserted end-relative cycle. The opened def-relative-singular-homology requires the representative's boundary to lie in the relative subspace. [Bigelow 2002, section 3.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0204057) distinguishes puncture-ended squares, boundary-ended squares, and mixed-endpoint squares by their respective relative groups.

The page describes B_n → S_n as a representation 'whose kernel is the nontrivial pure braid group' without restricting n. The companion construction includes n=1, where B1 and S1 are trivial, so this kernel is trivial. The opened cex-a-linear-representation-need-not-be-faithful correctly states 'Given: n≥2' before constructing its nontrivial kernel element σ1². That essential restriction is missing from the page's claim.
